# Migrate from SDK 0.x to SDK 2.x

## Upgrade the package and stay on v0

Upgrading to SDK 2.x does not move your workloads to v2. Use the root client’s
`.v0` namespace to keep calling the v0 platform. Resource imports move to the
v0 module, and so do the shared error classes (`DaytonaError`,
`DaytonaNotFoundError`, …). Client and configuration imports stay at the root.

The v0 error classes keep the 0.x constructor and fields, and every error the
`.v0` client raises is one of them, so `except` / `catch` code works as before.
The 2.x root error classes are markers that also catch v2 errors but take only a
message and carry no 0.x fields: when you move calls to `.v2`, import the errors
from the root again.

The root `Daytona()` constructor no longer checks for missing credentials: the
v0 client is built, and a missing API key reported, on the first `.v0` access (a
rejected key still fails on the first request, as in 0.x). If your code wraps
the constructor in `try` to detect missing credentials, access `.v0` inside that
`try`; the upgrade tool marks these constructions with a FIXME.

| Language | Before | SDK 2.x, same platform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python | `daytona.create()` | `daytona.v0.create()` |
| Python | `from daytona import Sandbox` | `from daytona.v0 import Sandbox` |
| TypeScript | `daytona.create()` | `daytona.v0.create()` |
| TypeScript | `import { Sandbox } from '@daytonaio/sdk'` | `import { Sandbox } from '@daytona/sdk/v0'` |

Install the SDK release you migrate to, with the v0 SDK extra for Python. Until SDK 2.0.0
is out, that is the exact alpha, e.g. `uv add 'daytona[v0-sdk]==2.0.0aN'` and
`npm install @daytona/sdk@2.0.0-alpha.N`; after it, `uv add 'daytona[v0-sdk]>=2,<3'` and
`npm install @daytona/sdk@^2.0.0`.
SDK 2.x targets Daytona Cloud. For a custom API URL, stay on SDK 0.x.

Python only: `DaytonaConfig` is a dataclass in SDK 2.x, not a pydantic model:
replace `model_dump()`/`dict()` with `dataclasses.asdict(cfg)`,
`model_copy()`/`copy()` with `dataclasses.replace(cfg, …)`, and
`model_validate()`/`parse_obj()` with `DaytonaConfig(**data)`.

Run the migration tool from your project directory:

```sh
npx @daytona/upgrade  # TypeScript or JavaScript
uvx daytona-upgrade  # Python
```

Each tool release migrates to the SDK release of the same version. Until SDK 2.0.0
is out, run the exact alpha you are migrating to, e.g. `npx @daytona/upgrade@2.0.0-alpha.N`
or `uvx daytona-upgrade@2.0.0aN`.

The tools update dependencies and proven client calls. Review each
`FIXME(daytona-upgrade)` item before running the result.

## Move a workflow to v2

Move one sandbox workflow at a time. Do not mix v0 and v2 handles within a
workflow. Run either tool with `--suggest-v2` to add suggestions without
rewriting calls or dependencies. Use `--remove-suggestions` to remove them.

<a id="data"></a>

### What does not carry over to v2

- Sandbox IDs and preview URLs are not preserved when a sandbox is imported to v2: code that stores or passes IDs needs the new ones.
- v0 snapshots appear in v2 as images and convert on first use, so the first sandbox created from one takes longer.
- Volumes migrate separately from sandboxes.
- A sandbox created on v0 can only be used through .v0: move every call in this workflow to v2 together.

In the tables, `{client}` is the root client (for example, `daytona`), and
`{sandbox}` is a v2 sandbox. Other identifiers stand for your values or handles.
The call forms show arguments to review, not automatic replacements. In Python,
await async operations, but not synchronous handle-binding calls. Sync clients
use the same method names.
In TypeScript, await asynchronous calls. `none` means no equivalent SDK method;
the notes describe an alternative where one exists.

## `client`

Python: close exists only on AsyncDaytona; all other listed method names match between sync and async

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.create(...)` | `{client}.v2.create(image, region=region)` | differs; create() makes ephemeral Linux sandboxes; stop, start and pause apply to macOS sandboxes; keep existing 0.x lifecycle workflows on .v0; image is optional and otherwise uses the platform default; v0 snapshot names become v2 image references; a v2 snapshot boots with create_from_snapshot(snapshot); Translate target to region and rebuild creation parameters, resource units (one resources=Resources(...) entry; memory and disk in GiB) and lifecycle settings; v0 timeout was the wait for the sandbox to start (0 = no limit); in v2 that wait is wait_seconds (default 60), and wait_seconds=0 returns without waiting; the suggested create keeps v2's 60-second wait, so to keep a 0.x budget, add wait_seconds=0 to it and wait once with that budget (sandbox.wait(until="started", timeout=0 if timeout is None else timeout), where 0 waits without a deadline); wait_seconds is whole seconds; create_timeout_seconds is the server budget before it deletes a sandbox that never starts; v0 create raised when the sandbox failed to start; v2 create returns the sandbox however its wait ends (check sandbox.state and sandbox.error), and that single wait raises on a terminal state (await it on AsyncDaytona); Image builds use create_from_build(builder, ...) instead of passing a v0 Image; v0 Image methods map to ImageBuilder: Image.base(ref) is ImageBuilder.from_registry(ref) and Image.debian_slim(version) is ImageBuilder.debian_slim(version); pip_install, run_commands, env, workdir, user, cmd, entrypoint, add_local_file, add_local_dir and pip_install_from_requirements keep their names (pip options such as find_links move into a run_commands line, and env takes a mapping or a name and a value); Image.from_dockerfile(path) becomes images.build_from_context(<the Dockerfile's directory>, dockerfile=...) or ImageBuilder.from_dockerfile(<its text>) when it copies no local files; pip_install_from_pyproject(path) becomes add_local_dir(<project directory>, "/app").run_commands("python -m pip install /app"); dockerfile_commands(lines) becomes run_commands, env and workdir steps, or from_dockerfile; signatures changed with the move: cmd(...) and entrypoint(...) take the arguments rather than a list (cmd("python", "app.py")), run_commands takes strings, debian_slim supports Python 3.10 to 3.14, and add_local_dir now honours the directory's .dockerignore; When replacing Image.from_dockerfile(path) with images.build_from_context(directory), it uploads the whole directory except what .dockerignore excludes (0.x uploaded only the COPY sources), so add a .dockerignore for secrets and large files; A registry image string such as "python:3.12" is not a v2 create source (IMAGE_NOT_FOUND); use create_from_build(ImageBuilder.from_registry(...)) or register the image first |
| `client.delete(...)` | `{client}.v2.delete(sandbox, timeout=60 if timeout is None else timeout)` | differs; Accepts a v2 sandbox or ID; Waits until the sandbox is destroyed: timeout is keyword-only seconds (default 60; 0 waits without a deadline); v0 delete(wait=False) returned at once; v2 always waits, so pass a short timeout and handle RequestTimeoutError if you must not block |
| `client.get(...)` | `{client}.v2.get(sandbox_id)` | differs; get accepts an ID, not a name; find_by_name(name, region=...) returns a tuple; No per-call request_timeout argument |
| `client.list(...)` | `{client}.v2.search(labels=labels, cursor=cursor, limit=limit)` | differs; Returns one page with items and next_cursor, not an iterator; list(cursor=, limit=) takes no filters; filtered queries (labels, states, region, ...) use search(), which is eventually consistent; Translate ListSandboxesQuery filters to search() keywords (states take SDK states such as "started"); async calls now await a page instead of yielding sandboxes; Use iter() for automatic unfiltered pagination |
| `client.start(...)` | `{client}.v2.start(sandbox, timeout=0 if timeout is None else timeout)` | differs; timeout is keyword-only and must be a number: v0's None (wait without limit) is 0 in v2; Accepts a v2 macOS sandbox or ID and resumes it if paused |
| `client.stop(...)` | `{client}.v2.stop(sandbox, timeout=0 if timeout is None else timeout)` | differs; Accepts a v2 sandbox or ID; Stop applies to macOS sandboxes; keep existing 0.x stop and start workflows on .v0, or delete an ephemeral Linux sandbox instead; Waits until stopped: timeout is keyword-only seconds (default 60; 0 waits without a deadline); there is no force argument |

## `client.volume`

Python: sync and async method names match

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.volume.create(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.create(name=name)` | differs; Creates a v2 volume of the server's default type; migrate v0 volume data separately; Optional type chooses disk or bucket, and size_gib sets a disk volume's capacity in GiB; on AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited; Review the volume type: v0 volumes were always disk volumes, v2 lets the server choose, so pass type="disk" (with size_gib) to keep a disk volume |
| `client.volume.delete(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.delete(volume_id)` | differs; Pass a v2 volume name or ID rather than a v0 Volume object; delete attached sandboxes first; Requests deletion without waiting for completion; on AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited |
| `client.volume.get(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.get(name_or_id, create=create)` | differs; Looks up a v2 volume by name or ID; create=True creates a volume of the server's default type if missing; Migrate v0 volume data separately; on AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited; Review the volume type: v0 volumes were always disk volumes, create=True lets the server choose, so to keep a disk volume call volumes.get(name_or_id) and, when it raises NotFoundError, volumes.create(name=..., type="disk") |
| `client.volume.list(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.list()` | differs; Returns one envelope page with items and next_cursor; use volumes.iter() to traverse all pages; On AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.volume.create(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.create({ name })` | differs; Creates a v2 volume of the server's default type; migrate v0 volume data separately; Optional type in the options object chooses disk or bucket, and sizeGib sets a disk volume's capacity in GiB; Review the volume type: v0 volumes were always disk volumes, v2 lets the server choose, so pass type: 'disk' (with sizeGib) to keep a disk volume |
| `client.volume.delete(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.delete(volumeId)` | differs; Pass a v2 volume name or ID rather than a v0 Volume object; delete attached sandboxes first; Requests deletion without waiting for completion |
| `client.volume.get(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.get(nameOrId, { create })` | differs; Looks up a v2 volume by name or ID; create: true creates a volume of the server's default type if missing; Migrate v0 volume data separately; Review the volume type: v0 volumes were always disk volumes, create: true lets the server choose, so to keep a disk volume call volumes.get(nameOrId) and, when it throws NotFoundError, volumes.create({ name, type: 'disk' }) |
| `client.volume.list(...)` | `{client}.v2.volumes.list()` | differs; Returns one envelope page with items and nextCursor; use volumes.iter() to traverse all pages |

## `client.secret`

Python: sync and async method names match

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.secret.create(...)` | `{client}.v2.secrets.set(name, value, allowed_domains=domains, description=description, if_not_exists=True)` | differs; Secrets become project-scoped; set returns Secret metadata without the write-only value; Translate hosts to explicit allowed_domains; unrestricted access requires an intentional ["*"]; if_not_exists preserves create-only behavior |
| `client.secret.delete(...)` | `{client}.v2.secrets.delete(name)` | differs; Uses the project secret name instead of its v0 ID |
| `client.secret.get(...)` | `{client}.v2.secrets.get(name)` | differs; Uses the project secret name instead of its v0 ID; Returns metadata without the secret value |
| `client.secret.list(...)` | `{client}.v2.secrets.list()` | differs; Lists project secret metadata in ListResult.items, with next_cursor; Pages with cursor and limit; no name, sort or order arguments |
| `client.secret.update(...)` | `{client}.v2.secrets.set(name, value, allowed_domains=domains, description=description)` | differs; Uses a project secret name rather than a v0 ID and returns Secret metadata without the write-only value; set requires value and allowed_domains; v0 partial updates cannot be copied unchanged; Metadata-only updates require supplying the write-only value again; get cannot recover it |

## `sandbox`

Python: sync and async method names match; create_lsp_server is synchronous even on AsyncSandbox and returns an AsyncLspServer

v2 fork waits for the new sandbox with a wait_seconds / waitSeconds budget in seconds (default 60; 0 returns once the fork is accepted) and returns the fork however the wait ends

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.archive(...)` | None | none; No v2 equivalent; keep 0.x archive workflows on .v0 |
| `sandbox.create_lsp_server(...)` | `{sandbox}.lsp.start(language_id, path_to_project)` | differs; Starts the server immediately instead of constructing a server for a later start call; On AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited; v0 AsyncSandbox.create_lsp_server was synchronous |
| `sandbox.create_snapshot(...)` | `{sandbox}.capture_image(name=name)` | differs; V0 filesystem snapshots correspond to v2 images; Returns an Image and has no timeout argument; Returns before the image is ready; wait with daytona.v2.images.get(image.id, wait="ready", timeout=timeout), which returns the image once it settles ("ready", "failed" or "error"; check that it is "ready" before booting from it) and raises RequestTimeoutError when the budget runs out; V2 create_snapshot(name) captures sandbox state and is a different operation |
| `sandbox._experimental_create_snapshot(...)` | `{sandbox}.capture_image(name=name)` | differs; Deprecated alias of create_snapshot in 0.x; V0 filesystem snapshots correspond to v2 images; Returns an Image and has no timeout argument; Returns before the image is ready; wait with daytona.v2.images.get(image.id, wait="ready", timeout=timeout), which returns the image once it settles ("ready", "failed" or "error"; check that it is "ready" before booting from it) and raises RequestTimeoutError when the budget runs out; V2 create_snapshot(name) captures sandbox state and is a different operation |
| `sandbox.create_ssh_access(...)` | None | none; No equivalent v0 SSH access-token management helper; V2 scoped access tokens are a different credential model |
| `sandbox.delete(...)` | `{sandbox}.delete(timeout=60 if timeout is None else timeout)` | differs; Waits until the sandbox is destroyed: timeout is keyword-only seconds (default 60; 0 waits without a deadline); v0 delete(wait=False) returned at once; v2 always waits, so pass a short timeout and handle RequestTimeoutError if you must not block |
| `sandbox.download_url(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.presigned_download_url(path, expires_in_seconds=ttl_seconds)` | differs; Moves to fs and renames the TTL argument; Omit expires_in_seconds when v0 ttl_seconds was None; v0 ttl_seconds <= 0 creates never-expiring links; v2 has no equivalent and requires an integer from 1 to 604800 (7 days), rejecting longer TTLs too; Requires a sandbox handle |
| `sandbox.expire_signed_preview_url(...)` | `{sandbox}.ports.expire_signed_preview_link(port, token)` | differs; Moves to the ports namespace; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.fork(...)` | `{sandbox}.fork(name=name, memory=False, wait_seconds=30 * 86_400 if timeout in (None, 0) else timeout)` | differs; memory=False preserves v0 filesystem-only cloning; v2 otherwise includes memory; name, memory and wait_seconds are keyword-only; wait_seconds is seconds and defaults to 60, like v0, so omit it when the 0.x call omitted timeout; wait_seconds=0 returns once the fork is accepted, while a v0 timeout of 0 or None waited without a deadline; v2 reads a wait_seconds above about 24.8 days (the timer maximum) as no deadline, so the suggestion passes 30 days for those; however the wait ends, the fork is returned: check fork.state; Only running sources start the fork automatically; paused or stopped sources require resume or start |

| `sandbox.get_metrics_latest(...)` | `{sandbox}.metrics()` | differs; Returns the v2 SystemMetrics model rather than SandboxMetrics; update field and unit handling |
| `sandbox.get_preview_link(...)` | `{sandbox}.ports.preview_link(port)` | differs; Moves to ports and returns a v2 PreviewLink; Private links include an access token; preview_link exposes the port if needed |
| `sandbox.create_signed_preview_url(...)` | `{sandbox}.ports.signed_preview_link(port, expires_in_seconds=expires_in_seconds)` | differs; Moves to ports; expires_in_seconds is keyword-only; Returns SignedPreviewLink with url, token and expires_at |

| `sandbox.get_user_root_dir(...)` | None | none; Deprecated v0 alias for get_user_home_dir; no v2 counterpart |
| `sandbox.get_work_dir(...)` | None | none; No v2 working-directory helper |
| `sandbox.pause(...)` | `{sandbox}.pause(timeout=timeout)` | differs; timeout is keyword-only; Requires a macOS sandbox; keep existing 0.x pause workflows on .v0 |

| `sandbox.rotate_signing_key(...)` | `{sandbox}.rotate_signing_key()` | differs; Requires a sandbox handle |
| `sandbox.set_auto_archive_interval(...)` | None | none; No v2 equivalent; keep 0.x auto-archive workflows on .v0 |

<a id="sandbox-fs"></a>
## `sandbox.fs`

Python: async methods require await; async transfer progress callbacks may be awaitable

Python: async upload_file_stream additionally accepts AsyncIterable[bytes]

Python and TypeScript: v2 filesystem transfers do not accept the v0 positional timeout

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.fs.create_folder(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.mkdir(path, mode=mode)` | differs; mode becomes keyword-only; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.delete_file(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.remove(path, recursive=recursive)` | differs; recursive becomes keyword-only; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.download_file(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.download_file(remote_path, local_path)` | differs; The disk-transfer form requires local_path; timeout is removed; For the bytes-returning overload use fs.read_bytes(remote_path); v2 does not create missing local parent directories; create them first |
| `sandbox.fs.download_file_stream(...)` | None | none; No chunk-iterator download method; Use fs.download_file(remote_path, local_path) for streaming to disk; For a custom HTTP stream use fs.presigned_download_url(remote_path) |
| `sandbox.fs.download_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.read_many(paths)` | differs; Convert FileDownloadRequest objects to remote path strings; timeout is removed; Returns BulkReadResult with files and errors, buffering contents in memory; For local destinations call fs.download_file(remote_path, local_path) per file; v0 created missing local parent directories; v2 does not, so create them first |
| `sandbox.fs.find_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.grep(path, pattern)` | differs; Read matches from result.items; each match is a FileMatch with file, line and content attributes; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.get_file_info(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.stat(path)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.list_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.list(path, depth=depth)` | differs; Read entries from result.items; depth becomes keyword-only; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.move_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.move(source, destination)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.replace_in_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.replace(files, pattern, new_value)` | differs; Read replacement results from result.items; each result is a ReplaceResult with file, success and error attributes; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.search_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.glob(path, pattern)` | differs; Read matching paths from result.items; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.set_file_permissions(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.chmod(path, mode=mode, owner=owner, group=group)` | differs; mode, owner and group become keyword-only; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.upload_file(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.upload_file(local_path, remote_path)` | differs; For the bytes overload use fs.write_bytes(remote_path, content); timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.upload_file_stream(...)` | None | none; No arbitrary file-like or AsyncIterable upload method; Use fs.upload_file(local_path, remote_path) for a streamed local file; For custom streaming use fs.presigned_upload_url(remote_path) |
| `sandbox.fs.upload_files(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.write_many(files_by_path)` | differs; Convert FileUpload entries to a remote-path-to-bytes mapping; timeout is removed; Returns BulkWriteResult with files and errors; For local source paths call fs.upload_file(local_path, remote_path) per file |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.fs.createFolder(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.mkdir(path, { mode })` | differs; mode moves into an options object |
| `sandbox.fs.deleteFile(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.remove(path, { recursive })` | differs; recursive moves into an options object |
| `sandbox.fs.downloadFile(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.downloadFile(remotePath, localPath)` | differs; The disk-transfer form requires localPath; positional timeout is removed; For the buffer-returning overload use fs.readBytes(remotePath), which returns Uint8Array; v2 does not create missing local parent directories; create them first |
| `sandbox.fs.downloadFileStream(...)` | None | none; No Readable-returning download method; Use fs.downloadFile(remotePath, localPath) for streaming to disk; For a custom HTTP stream use fs.presignedDownloadUrl(remotePath) |
| `sandbox.fs.downloadFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.readMany(paths)` | differs; Convert download request objects to remote path strings; positional timeout is removed; Returns BulkReadResult with files and errors, buffering contents in memory; For local destinations call fs.downloadFile(remotePath, localPath) per file; v0 created missing local parent directories; v2 does not, so create them first |
| `sandbox.fs.findFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.grep(path, pattern)` | differs; Read matches from result.items |
| `sandbox.fs.getFileDetails(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.stat(path)` | differs; Renamed to stat; same argument, returns the v2 FileInfo type |
| `sandbox.fs.listFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.list(path, { depth })` | differs; Read entries from result.items |
| `sandbox.fs.moveFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.move(source, destination)` | differs; Renamed to move; same arguments |
| `sandbox.fs.replaceInFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.replace(files, pattern, newValue)` | differs; Read replacement results from result.items |
| `sandbox.fs.searchFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.glob(path, pattern)` | differs; Read matching paths from result.items |
| `sandbox.fs.setFilePermissions(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.chmod(path, permissions)` | differs; Renamed to chmod; the permissions object becomes FilePermissionsOptions |
| `sandbox.fs.uploadFile(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.uploadFile(localPath, remotePath)` | differs; For the Buffer overload use fs.writeBytes(remotePath, content); Positional timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.fs.uploadFileStream(...)` | None | none; No arbitrary Readable upload method; Use fs.uploadFile(localPath, remotePath) for a streamed local file; For custom streaming use fs.presignedUploadUrl(remotePath) |
| `sandbox.fs.uploadFiles(...)` | `{sandbox}.fs.writeMany(filesByPath)` | differs; Convert FileUpload entries to a remote-path-to-Uint8Array record; positional timeout is removed; Returns BulkWriteResult with files and errors; For local source paths call fs.uploadFile(localPath, remotePath) per file |

<a id="sandbox-git"></a>
## `sandbox.git`

Python: AsyncGit exposes the same method names with await

Python: v2 optional Git arguments are keyword-only

TypeScript: v2 groups optional Git arguments into options objects

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.git.add(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.add(path, files)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.git.branches(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.list_branches(path)` | differs; Read branch names from result.items; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.git.checkout_branch(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.checkout_branch(path, branch)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |

| `sandbox.git.get_config(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.get_config(key, scope=scope, path=path)` | differs; scope and path become keyword-only; request_timeout is removed; The "system" scope is gone: v2 accepts only "global" and "local" |
| `sandbox.git.init(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.init(path, bare=bare, initial_branch=initial_branch)` | differs; bare and initial_branch become keyword-only; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.git.pull(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.pull(path, username=username, password=password, branch=branch, remote=remote, timeout=request_timeout)` | differs; Optional arguments become keyword-only; request_timeout is replaced by timeout (seconds, one deadline for the whole operation); v0 request_timeout=0 (no limit) becomes timeout=0, and omitting timeout selects the 30-minute default |
| `sandbox.git.push(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.push(path, username=username, password=password, branch=branch, remote=remote, set_upstream=set_upstream, timeout=request_timeout)` | differs; Optional arguments become keyword-only; request_timeout is replaced by timeout (seconds, one deadline for the whole operation); v0 request_timeout=0 (no limit) becomes timeout=0, and omitting timeout selects the 30-minute default |
| `sandbox.git.remote_add(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.add_remote(path, name, url)` | differs; fetch, overwrite and request_timeout are not accepted; Use process.run for Git CLI behavior requiring fetch or overwrite |

| `sandbox.git.status(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.status(path)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.git.add(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.add(path, files)` | differs; Same name and arguments on the v2 sandbox git service |
| `sandbox.git.branches(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.listBranches(path)` | differs; Read branch names from result.items |

| `sandbox.git.pull(...)` | `{sandbox}.git.pull(path, { username, password, branch, remote })` | differs; Optional arguments move into an options object |

<a id="sandbox-process"></a>
## `sandbox.process`

Python: async and sync method names match; async PTY create/connect require on_data while sync variants do not

TypeScript: v0 and v2 process timeouts both take seconds; v2 names them timeoutSeconds and executionTimeoutSeconds

TypeScript: getSessionCommandLogs and getEntrypointLogs each have collected and callback-streaming overloads

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.process.code_run(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.run(code, language=language, isolated=True, env=env, timeout=timeout)` | differs; Select the language explicitly rather than relying on the v0 sandbox language; CodeRunParams.env becomes env; argv has no interpreter equivalent; Returns InterpreterResult rather than ExecuteResponse and execution artifacts |
| `sandbox.process.connect_pty_session(...)` | `handle = {sandbox}.pty.connect(pty_id)` | differs; connect returns a process handle without opening a WebSocket; Use handle.stream_logs() for output and handle.write_stdin(data) for input; Python v2 has no bundled PTY attach; supply a custom WebSocket adapter if you need a socket |
| `sandbox.process.create_pty_session(...)` | `handle = {sandbox}.pty.start(name=pty_name, cwd=cwd, env=envs, terminal=TerminalSize(cols=cols, rows=rows))` | differs; v0 id becomes a name alias; the process receives a new generated id; pty_size becomes terminal=TerminalSize(cols=..., rows=...) (import TerminalSize from daytona.v2); omitted, it is 80 by 24; Replace on_data or handle iteration with handle.stream_logs(); On AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited |
| `sandbox.process.create_session(...)` | `session = {sandbox}.process.create_session(name=session_id)` | differs; Returns a Session handle instead of None; request_timeout is removed; The supplied id becomes a name alias; retain session.id; Set shared cwd and env when creating the session; On AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited |
| `sandbox.process.delete_session(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect_session(session_id).delete()` | differs; Ends the shell and removes its command records; request_timeout is removed; Prefer the retained Session handle's delete() |
| `sandbox.process.exec(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, execution_timeout=timeout)` | differs; cwd and env become keyword-only; timeout becomes execution_timeout, not the caller wait timeout; Read output or stdout instead of result; Check the returned reason as well as exit_code |
| `sandbox.process.execute_session_command(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect_session(session_id).run(command, timeout=timeout)` | differs; Extract command from SessionExecuteRequest; suppress_input_echo has no matching option; For run_async=True use session.start(command), which returns a ProcessHandle; v0 timeout bounded only the wait and maps to timeout; 0.x had no command deadline, so pass execution_timeout to stop the command; The result is a ProcessResult: v0 cmd_id becomes process_id |
| `sandbox.process.get_entrypoint_logs(...)` | `{sandbox}.entrypoint_logs()` | differs; Moved from process to the sandbox handle; Returns the combined entrypoint output as one text; v0 returned separate stdout/stderr fields |
| `sandbox.process.get_entrypoint_logs_async(...)` | None | none; No dedicated v2 entrypoint-session log stream; For a process you start iterate handle.stream_logs(): a StreamLogFrameEvent (type "log") carries the frame, routed by frame.channel |
| `sandbox.process.get_entrypoint_session(...)` | None | none; No dedicated v2 entrypoint shell-session resource; Create an explicit session with process.create_session() when persistent shell state is needed |
| `sandbox.process.get_pty_session_info(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.connect(pty_id).get()` | differs; Returns ProcessInfo rather than PtySessionInfo; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.process.get_session(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect_session(session_id).get()` | differs; Returns shell ProcessInfo rather than command history; request_timeout is removed; For commands use process.list(session_id=session.id); connect_session only binds identity; get() fetches metadata |
| `sandbox.process.get_session_command(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.get(command_id)` | differs; Use the v2 command handle's id; no session_id argument is needed; Returns ProcessInfo rather than Command; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.process.get_session_command_logs(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect(command_id).logs()` | differs; Returns a cursor-based page of channel-tagged log frames; session_id and request_timeout are removed |
| `sandbox.process.get_session_command_logs_async(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect(command_id).stream_logs()` | differs; Iterate StreamLogEvent values instead of passing output callbacks: type "log" events carry a LogFrame on .frame, routed by frame.channel; state, warning and eof events follow; Use async for with AsyncProcessHandle and for with its sync twin; No session_id argument is needed |
| `sandbox.process.kill_pty_session(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.delete(pty_id)` | differs; Stops the PTY and removes its process record and retained logs; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.process.list_pty_sessions(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.list()` | differs; Read ProcessInfo rows from result.items; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.process.list_sessions(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.list(kind="session")` | differs; Read shell process metadata from result.items; request_timeout is removed; Bind an item with process.connect_session(item.id) |
| `sandbox.process.resize_pty_session(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.connect(pty_id).resize(cols, rows)` | differs; Expand PtySize into cols and rows; request_timeout is removed; Returns None rather than PtySessionInfo |
| `sandbox.process.send_session_command_input(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect(command_id).write_stdin(data)` | differs; Start the command with session.start(command, stdin="open"); Use the returned command handle's id; session_id and request_timeout are removed; Open stdin when starting the command before sending input |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.process.codeRun(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.run(code, { language, isolated: true, env, timeoutSeconds: timeout })` | differs; Select the language explicitly rather than relying on the v0 sandbox language; CodeRunParams.env becomes env; argv has no interpreter equivalent; Returns InterpreterResult; timeout becomes timeoutSeconds (still seconds) |
| `sandbox.process.connectPty(...)` | `const handle = {sandbox}.pty.connect(ptyId); const connection = await handle.attach()` | differs; connect returns a process handle without opening a WebSocket; Replace onData with iteration over connection.readable; Connection options are not accepted by pty.connect |
| `sandbox.process.createPty(...)` | `const handle = await {sandbox}.pty.start(undefined, { name: ptyName, cwd, env: envs, terminal: { cols, rows } }); const connection = await handle.attach()` | differs; v0 id becomes a name alias; the process receives a new generated id; Terminal dimensions move into terminal; Replace onData with iteration over connection.readable |
| `sandbox.process.createSession(...)` | `const session = await {sandbox}.process.createSession({ name: sessionId })` | differs; Returns a Session handle instead of void; The supplied id becomes a name alias; retain session.id; Set shared cwd and env when creating the session |
| `sandbox.process.deleteSession(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connectSession(sessionId).delete()` | differs; Ends the shell and removes its command records; Prefer the retained Session handle's delete() |
| `sandbox.process.executeCommand(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.run(command, { cwd, env, executionTimeoutSeconds: timeout })` | differs; Move cwd and env into options; timeout becomes executionTimeoutSeconds (still seconds), not the caller wait timeout; Read output or stdout instead of result; Check the returned reason as well as exitCode |
| `sandbox.process.executeSessionCommand(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connectSession(sessionId).run(command, { timeoutSeconds: timeout })` | differs; Extract command from SessionExecuteRequest; For runAsync=true use session.start(command), which returns a ProcessHandle; v0 timeout bounded only the wait and maps to timeoutSeconds (seconds); 0.x had no command deadline, so pass executionTimeoutSeconds to stop the command; suppressInputEcho has no matching option; The result is a ProcessResult: v0 cmdId becomes processId |
| `sandbox.process.getEntrypointLogs(...)` | `{sandbox}.entrypointLogs()` | differs; Moved from process to the sandbox handle; Returns the combined entrypoint output as one text; v0 returned separate stdout/stderr fields; The callback-streaming overload has no v2 equivalent; v2 returns the log once as a string |
| `sandbox.process.getEntrypointSession(...)` | None | none; No dedicated v2 entrypoint shell-session resource; Create an explicit session with process.createSession() when persistent shell state is needed |
| `sandbox.process.getPtySessionInfo(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.connect(ptyId).get()` | differs; Returns ProcessInfo rather than PtySessionInfo |
| `sandbox.process.getSession(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connectSession(sessionId).get()` | differs; Returns shell ProcessInfo rather than a session containing command history; For commands use process.list({ sessionId: session.id }); connectSession only binds identity; get() fetches metadata |
| `sandbox.process.getSessionCommand(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.get(commandId)` | differs; Use the v2 command handle's id; no sessionId argument is needed; Returns ProcessInfo rather than Command |
| `sandbox.process.getSessionCommandLogs(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect(commandId).logs()` | differs; Returns a cursor-based page of channel-tagged log frames; For the callback-streaming overload use handle.streamLogs(); Route log events by frame.channel instead of onStdout and onStderr callbacks |
| `sandbox.process.killPtySession(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.delete(ptyId)` | differs; Stops the PTY and removes its process record and retained logs |
| `sandbox.process.listPtySessions(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.list()` | differs; Read ProcessInfo rows from result.items |
| `sandbox.process.listSessions(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.list({ kind: 'session' })` | differs; Read shell process metadata from result.items; Bind an item with process.connectSession(item.id) |
| `sandbox.process.resizePtySession(...)` | `{sandbox}.pty.connect(ptyId).resize(cols, rows)` | differs; Returns void rather than PtySessionInfo |
| `sandbox.process.sendSessionCommandInput(...)` | `{sandbox}.process.connect(commandId).writeStdin(data)` | differs; Start the command with session.start(command, { stdin: 'open' }); Use the returned command handle's id, not the shell session id; Open stdin when starting the command before sending input |

<a id="sandbox-code-interpreter"></a>
## `sandbox.code_interpreter` / `sandbox.codeInterpreter`

Python: AsyncCodeInterpreter exposes the same method names with await

Python and TypeScript: v0 contexts are generated metadata DTOs rather than executable SDK handles

TypeScript: v0 and v2 interpreter timeouts both take seconds; v2 names it timeoutSeconds

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.code_interpreter.create_context(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.create_context(language="python", cwd=cwd)` | differs; Language is explicit and cwd becomes keyword-only; Returns an executable InterpreterContext handle |
| `sandbox.code_interpreter.delete_context(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.delete_context(context)` | differs; Pass a v2 context handle, serialized identity or context id; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.code_interpreter.list_contexts(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.list_contexts()` | differs; Returns executable context handles rather than v0 metadata DTOs; Lists language-kernel contexts, including default contexts that exist; request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.code_interpreter.run_code(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.run(code, language="python", context=context, timeout=timeout)` | differs; Pass a v2 context handle; omitted context uses the default Python context; No on_stdout, on_stderr or on_error callbacks; inspect InterpreterResult; envs becomes env, but per-run env is refused with an explicit context |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.codeInterpreter.createContext(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.createContext({ language: 'python', cwd })` | differs; Language is explicit and cwd moves into an options object; Returns an executable InterpreterContext handle |
| `sandbox.codeInterpreter.deleteContext(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.deleteContext(context)` | differs; Pass a v2 context handle, serialized identity or context id |
| `sandbox.codeInterpreter.listContexts(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.listContexts()` | differs; Returns executable context handles rather than v0 metadata DTOs; Lists language-kernel contexts, including default contexts that exist |
| `sandbox.codeInterpreter.runCode(...)` | `{sandbox}.interpreter.run(code, { language: 'python', context, timeoutSeconds: timeout })` | differs; Pass a v2 context handle; timeout becomes timeoutSeconds (still seconds); No onStdout, onStderr or onError callbacks; inspect InterpreterResult; envs becomes env, but per-run env is refused with an explicit context |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use` / `sandbox.computerUse`

Python: v2 removes request_timeout from all computer-use calls

Python: v2 response objects are dataclasses rather than generated Pydantic models

v2 moves process operations under the computer-use service attribute

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.start(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.start()` | differs; Returns ComputerUseLifecycleResponse instead of ComputerUseStartResponse; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.stop(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.stop()` | differs; Returns ComputerUseLifecycleResponse instead of ComputerUseStopResponse; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.get_status(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.status()` | differs; Returns a discriminated desktop status with desktop and optional failure cause; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.get_process_status(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.service.status(process_name)` | differs; Moves under service and returns ComputerUseProcessRunningStatus; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.restart_process(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.service.restart(process_name)` | differs; Moves under service and returns ComputerUseProcessRestartResponse; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.get_process_logs(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.service.logs(process_name)` | differs; Moves under service and returns ComputerUseProcessLogsResponse; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.get_process_errors(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.service.errors(process_name)` | differs; Moves under service and returns ComputerUseProcessErrorsResponse; request_timeout is no longer accepted |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.start(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.start()` | differs; Returns a lifecycle response with required message and process-status fields |
| `sandbox.computerUse.stop(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.stop()` | differs; Returns a lifecycle response with required message and process-status fields |
| `sandbox.computerUse.getStatus(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.status()` | differs; Returns a discriminated desktop status with desktop and optional failure cause |
| `sandbox.computerUse.getProcessStatus(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.service.status(processName)` | differs; Moves under service and returns required processName and running fields |
| `sandbox.computerUse.restartProcess(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.service.restart(processName)` | differs; Moves under service and returns required message and processName fields |
| `sandbox.computerUse.getProcessLogs(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.service.logs(processName)` | differs; Moves under service and returns required logs and processName fields |
| `sandbox.computerUse.getProcessErrors(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.service.errors(processName)` | differs; Moves under service and returns required errors and processName fields |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-mouse"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.mouse` / `sandbox.computerUse.mouse`

Python: v2 action arguments are keyword-only and request_timeout is removed

TypeScript: v2 actions accept request objects instead of positional arguments

v2 has no down/up methods, click counts, mouse modifiers or horizontal scrolling

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.get_position(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.mouse.position()` | differs; Returns a ComputerUsePoint dataclass with required x and y; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.move(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.mouse.move(x=x, y=y)` | differs; Coordinates become keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; Returns a ComputerUsePoint dataclass |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.down(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for holding a mouse button down; click or drag cannot preserve arbitrary down/move/up sequences |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.up(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for releasing a held mouse button |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.click(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.mouse.click(x=x, y=y, button=button, double=double)` | differs; Arguments become keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; v2 has no clicks or modifiers parameters; Returns a ComputerUsePoint dataclass |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.drag(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.mouse.drag(start_x=start_x, start_y=start_y, end_x=end_x, end_y=end_y, button=button)` | differs; Arguments become keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; v2 has no modifiers parameter; Returns a ComputerUsePoint dataclass |
| `sandbox.computer_use.mouse.scroll(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.mouse.scroll(x=x, y=y, direction=direction, amount=amount)` | differs; Arguments become keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; Only up/down are supported and modifiers are unavailable; Returns a result object with success instead of bool |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.getPosition(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.mouse.position()` | differs; Returns required x and y fields instead of optional coordinates |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.move(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.mouse.move({ x, y })` | differs; Coordinates move into a request object; Returned coordinates are required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.down(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for holding a mouse button down; click or drag cannot preserve arbitrary down/move/up sequences |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.up(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for releasing a held mouse button |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.click(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.mouse.click({ x, y, button, double })` | differs; Arguments move into a request object; v2 has no clicks or modifiers parameters; Returned coordinates are required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.drag(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.mouse.drag({ startX, startY, endX, endY, button })` | differs; Arguments move into a request object; button is optional and defaults to 'left'; v2 has no modifiers parameter; Returned coordinates are required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.mouse.scroll(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.mouse.scroll({ x, y, direction, amount })` | differs; Arguments move into a request object; Only up/down are supported and modifiers are unavailable; Returns an object with success instead of boolean |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-keyboard"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard` / `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard`

Python: v2 arguments are keyword-only and request_timeout is removed

TypeScript: v2 actions accept request objects instead of positional arguments

v2 has no persistent key-down or key-up methods

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard.type(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.keyboard.type(text=text, delay=None if delay is None else delay / 1000)` | differs; Arguments become keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; delay is in seconds (v0 took milliseconds) |
| `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard.press(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.keyboard.key(key=key, modifiers=modifiers)` | differs; Renamed to key with keyword-only arguments and no request_timeout; Modifier types are restricted to ctrl, alt, shift and cmd |
| `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard.hotkey(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.keyboard.hotkey(keys=keys)` | differs; keys becomes keyword-only and request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard.down(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for holding a key down across operations |
| `sandbox.computer_use.keyboard.up(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for releasing a held key |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard.type(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.keyboard.type({ text, delaySeconds: delay === undefined ? undefined : delay / 1000 })` | differs; Text and delay move into a request object; delay becomes delaySeconds, in seconds (v0 took milliseconds) |
| `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard.press(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.keyboard.key({ key, modifiers })` | differs; Renamed to key with a request object; Modifier types are restricted to ctrl, alt, shift and cmd |
| `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard.hotkey(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.keyboard.hotkey({ keys })` | differs; The chord string moves into a request object's keys field |
| `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard.down(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for holding a key down across operations |
| `sandbox.computerUse.keyboard.up(...)` | None | none; v2 has no method for releasing a held key |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-screenshot"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.screenshot` / `sandbox.computerUse.screenshot`

v2 moves screenshots to the computer-use screen attribute

Python: v2 uses keyword-only arguments and dataclass responses without request_timeout

v2 compression format is restricted to png or jpeg

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.screenshot.take_full_screen(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.screen.screenshot(show_cursor=show_cursor)` | differs; Moves to screen.screenshot with keyword-only show_cursor; Returns a ComputerUseScreenshotResponse dataclass and removes request_timeout |
| `sandbox.computer_use.screenshot.take_region(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.screen.screenshot(region=ComputerUseRegion(x=region.x, y=region.y, width=region.width, height=region.height), show_cursor=show_cursor)` | differs; The region becomes a ComputerUseRegion (from daytona.v2 import ComputerUseRegion) passed as region= to screen.screenshot; Returns a ComputerUseScreenshotResponse dataclass and removes request_timeout |
| `sandbox.computer_use.screenshot.take_compressed(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.screen.screenshot(format=options.fmt, quality=options.quality, scale=options.scale, show_cursor=options.show_cursor)` | differs; Expand options into keyword-only arguments or omit them when options is None; Compression applies only when format, quality or scale is set; when options sets none of them, pass format="png" to keep a compressed image; Only png and jpeg formats are supported; Returns a ComputerUseScreenshotResponse dataclass and removes request_timeout |
| `sandbox.computer_use.screenshot.take_compressed_region(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.screen.screenshot(region=ComputerUseRegion(x=region.x, y=region.y, width=region.width, height=region.height), format=options.fmt, quality=options.quality, scale=options.scale, show_cursor=options.show_cursor)` | differs; Pass the region as a ComputerUseRegion (from daytona.v2 import ComputerUseRegion) and expand options into keyword-only arguments, omitting options fields when None; Compression applies only when format, quality or scale is set; when options sets none of them, pass format="png" to keep a compressed image; Only png and jpeg formats are supported; Returns a ComputerUseScreenshotResponse dataclass and removes request_timeout |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.screenshot.takeFullScreen(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.screen.screenshot({ showCursor })` | differs; Moves to screen.screenshot with an options object; The screenshot response field is required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.screenshot.takeRegion(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.screen.screenshot({ region, showCursor })` | differs; Region and showCursor merge into one screen.screenshot options object; The screenshot response field is required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.screenshot.takeCompressed(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.screen.screenshot(options)` | differs; Moves to screen.screenshot with format restricted to png or jpeg; Compression applies only when format, quality or scale is set; when options sets none of them, pass format: 'png' to keep a compressed image; The screenshot response field is required |
| `sandbox.computerUse.screenshot.takeCompressedRegion(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.screen.screenshot({ region, ...options })` | differs; Region and compression options merge into one screen.screenshot options object; Compression applies only when format, quality or scale is set; when options sets none of them, pass format: 'png' to keep a compressed image; Only png and jpeg formats are supported; The screenshot response field is required |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-display"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.display` / `sandbox.computerUse.display`

Python: v2 returns dataclasses and removes request_timeout

v2 requires display and window fields that were optional in v0

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.display.get_info(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.display.info()` | differs; Returns ComputerUseDisplayInfoResponse with required display fields; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.display.get_windows(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.display.windows()` | differs; Returns ComputerUseDisplayWindowsResponse with required window fields; request_timeout is no longer accepted |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.display.getInfo(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.display.info()` | differs; The displays array and each display's fields are required instead of optional |
| `sandbox.computerUse.display.getWindows(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.display.windows()` | differs; The windows array and each window's fields are required instead of optional |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-recording"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.recording` / `sandbox.computerUse.recording`

Python: v2 returns dataclasses and removes request_timeout

TypeScript: v2 start and stop accept request objects

v2 download returns bytes in Python or Uint8Array in TypeScript instead of streaming to a local path

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.start(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.start(label=label)` | differs; label becomes keyword-only and request_timeout is removed; Returns a ComputerUseRecording dataclass |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.stop(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.stop(id=recording_id)` | differs; recording_id becomes keyword-only id and request_timeout is removed; Returns a ComputerUseRecording dataclass |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.list(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.list()` | differs; Returns a ComputerUseRecordingsResponse dataclass containing recording dataclasses; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.get(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.get(recording_id)` | differs; Returns a ComputerUseRecording dataclass; The keyword recording_id becomes id and request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.delete(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.delete(recording_id)` | differs; The keyword recording_id becomes id and request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.computer_use.recording.download(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.recording.download(recording_id)` | differs; Returns bytes in memory instead of streaming to local_path; Write the returned bytes to the desired file separately; The keyword recording_id becomes id |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.start(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.start({ label })` | differs; The optional label moves into a request object |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.stop(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.stop({ id })` | differs; The recording ID moves into a request object's id field |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.list(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.list()` | differs; Returns ComputerUseRecordingsResponse instead of ListRecordingsResponse |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.get(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.get(id)` | differs; Same argument; returns ComputerUseRecording instead of Recording |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.delete(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.delete(id)` | differs; Same argument on the v2 recording namespace |
| `sandbox.computerUse.recording.download(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.recording.download(id)` | differs; Returns Uint8Array in memory instead of streaming to localPath; Write the returned bytes to the desired file separately |

<a id="sandbox-computer-use-accessibility"></a>
## `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility` / `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility`

v2 moves accessibility to the computer-use a11y attribute and requires explicit scope for tree and find

Python: v2 arguments are keyword-only

Python: v2 returns dataclasses and removes request_timeout

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility.get_tree(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.a11y.tree(scope=scope, pid=pid, max_depth=max_depth)` | differs; Moves to a11y.tree with keyword-only arguments and no request_timeout; scope is required and must be focused, pid or all; Returns a dataclass tree with required root and truncated fields |
| `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility.find_nodes(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.a11y.find(scope=scope, pid=pid, role=role, name=name, name_match=name_match, states=states, limit=limit)` | differs; Moves to a11y.find with keyword-only arguments and no request_timeout; scope is required and name_match is restricted to exact, substring or regex; Returns a dataclass result with required matches and truncated fields |
| `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility.focus_node(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.a11y.focus(id=node_id)` | differs; Moves to a11y.focus with keyword-only id instead of node_id; request_timeout is no longer accepted |
| `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility.invoke_node(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.a11y.invoke(id=node_id, action=action)` | differs; Moves to a11y.invoke with keyword-only id and action; node_id becomes id and request_timeout is removed |
| `sandbox.computer_use.accessibility.set_node_value(...)` | `{sandbox}.computer_use.a11y.set_value(id=node_id, value=value)` | differs; Moves to a11y.set_value with keyword-only id and value; node_id becomes id and request_timeout is removed |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility.getTree(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.a11y.tree({ scope, pid, maxDepth })` | differs; Moves to a11y.tree and requires scope to be focused, pid or all; Root and truncated are required and nodes include value and valueTruncated |
| `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility.findNodes(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.a11y.find({ scope, pid, role, name, nameMatch, states, limit })` | differs; Moves to a11y.find and requires scope to be focused, pid or all; nameMatch is restricted to exact, substring or regex; Matches and truncated are required and nodes include value and valueTruncated |
| `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility.focusNode(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.a11y.focus({ id })` | differs; Moves to a11y.focus with an object containing id |
| `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility.invokeNode(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.a11y.invoke({ id, action })` | differs; Moves to a11y.invoke with an object containing id and optional action |
| `sandbox.computerUse.accessibility.setNodeValue(...)` | `{sandbox}.computerUse.a11y.setValue({ id, value })` | differs; Moves to a11y.setValue with an object containing id and value |

<a id="lsp-server"></a>
## `lsp_server` / `lspServer`

Python: AsyncLspServer exposes the same method names with await

Python and TypeScript: retain the v2 handle returned by sandbox.lsp.start as lsp

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lsp_server.completions(...)` | `lsp.completions(uri, position)` | differs; Pass a file URI; v0 added the file:// prefix to path; Pass position as a dict {"line": p.line, "character": p.character} or a v2 LspPosition; a v0 LspCompletionPosition is rejected; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.did_close(...)` | `lsp.close_document(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.did_open(...)` | `lsp.open_document(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.document_symbols(...)` | `lsp.document_symbols(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.sandbox_symbols(...)` | `lsp.workspace_symbols(query)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.start(...)` | `lsp = {sandbox}.lsp.start(language_id, path_to_project)` | differs; Start through sandbox.lsp and retain the returned server handle; A v2 server handle has no start() method; request_timeout is removed; On AsyncDaytona this call must be awaited |
| `lsp_server.stop(...)` | `lsp.stop()` | differs; request_timeout is removed |
| `lsp_server.workspace_symbols(...)` | `lsp.workspace_symbols(query)` | differs; request_timeout is removed |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lspServer.completions(...)` | `lsp.completions(uri, position)` | differs; Pass a file URI; v0 added the file:// prefix to path |
| `lspServer.didClose(...)` | `lsp.closeDocument(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument |
| `lspServer.didOpen(...)` | `lsp.openDocument(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument |
| `lspServer.documentSymbols(...)` | `lsp.documentSymbols(uri)` | differs; Pass a file URI rather than the v0 path argument |
| `lspServer.sandboxSymbols(...)` | `lsp.workspaceSymbols(query)` | differs; Renamed to workspaceSymbols on the v2 LSP handle |
| `lspServer.start(...)` | `const lsp = await {sandbox}.lsp.start(languageId, pathToProject)` | differs; Start through sandbox.lsp and retain the returned server handle; A v2 server handle has no start() method |
| `lspServer.stop(...)` | `lsp.stop()` | differs; Same name on the v2 LSP handle |
| `lspServer.workspaceSymbols(...)` | `lsp.workspaceSymbols(query)` | differs; Same name and argument on the v2 LSP handle |

<a id="pty-handle"></a>
## `pty_handle` / `ptyHandle`

Python and TypeScript: retain the returned v2 process handle as handle; TypeScript attachment separately returns connection

Python: is_connected is synchronous on both classes; only sync wait accepts on_data and timeout and only sync wait_for_connection accepts timeout

Python: v2 attach requires an external WebSocket adapter; TypeScript: exitCode and error are properties, not methods

### Python

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pty_handle.disconnect(...)` | None | none; v2 process handles have no persistent WebSocket connection to disconnect; Close a custom WebSocket adapter separately; Python attach is not bundled |
| `pty_handle.is_connected(...)` | None | none; No SDK WebSocket-connected predicate; Track custom adapter state separately from handle.get() process state |
| `pty_handle.kill(...)` | `handle.delete()` | differs; Deletes the PTY process and retained logs, stopping it first; For signal-only behavior use handle.kill(signal="KILL") |
| `pty_handle.resize(...)` | `handle.resize(cols, rows)` | differs; Expand PtySize into separate cols and rows arguments; Returns None rather than PtySessionInfo |
| `pty_handle.send_input(...)` | `handle.write_stdin(data)` | direct |
| `pty_handle.wait(...)` | `handle.wait()` | differs; Returns WaitResult with reason rather than PtyResult with error; Output consumption is separate through handle.stream_logs(); For the v0 sync timeout argument use handle.wait(timeout=timeout) |
| `pty_handle.wait_for_connection(...)` | None | none; No bundled Python WebSocket attachment handshake; Use HTTP handle.write_stdin(data) and handle.stream_logs(), or supply a custom adapter |

### TypeScript

| v0 call | v2 equivalent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ptyHandle.disconnect(...)` | `connection.close()` | differs; Close the duplex connection returned by handle.attach(); This disconnects transport without deleting the process |
| `ptyHandle.isConnected(...)` | None | none; No duplex connected predicate; Track attachment lifecycle and readable completion separately from handle.get() process state |
| `ptyHandle.kill(...)` | `handle.delete()` | differs; Deletes the PTY process and retained logs, stopping it first; For signal-only behavior use handle.kill({ signal: 'KILL' }) |
| `ptyHandle.resize(...)` | `handle.resize(cols, rows)` | differs; Returns void rather than PtySessionInfo |
| `ptyHandle.sendInput(...)` | `handle.writeStdin(data)` | direct |
| `ptyHandle.wait(...)` | `handle.wait()` | differs; Returns WaitResult with reason rather than PtyResult with error; Consume connection.readable or handle.streamLogs() separately |
| `ptyHandle.waitForConnection(...)` | `const connection = await handle.attach()` | differs; attach opens and awaits a new WebSocket connection; Retain its duplex connection for reading, writing and closing |
